note.text: Stage 1. A seed holds a tiny baby plant (the embryo) and a store of food, wrapped in a tough seed coat.
note.remember: A seed is a baby plant with a packed lunch.

steps.title: Embryo
steps.instruction: Draw the curled embryo inside the seed.

note.text: With water and warmth, the embryo wakes up and starts to grow. This is called germination.

steps.title: Seedling
steps.instruction: Trace the seedling's first two leaves.

note.text: Stage 2. The first leaves (seed leaves) feed the seedling with food stored in the seed until true leaves grow.
note.remember: Roots grow down, the shoot grows up toward light.

steps.title: Stem and roots
steps.instruction: Draw the stem, the soil line and the roots.

note.text: Roots hold the plant in place and take in water and minerals. The stem carries them up to the leaves.
Stage 3. The adult plant makes its own food in its leaves, using sunlight, water and air.

steps.title: Stem
steps.instruction: Draw the stem and the soil line.

note.text: The stem holds the leaves and flowers up toward the light.
Flowers are how the plant reproduces. Bees and wind carry pollen between flowers: this is pollination.

steps.title: Flower center
steps.instruction: Draw the center of the flower.

note.text: The center holds the parts that make pollen and the part that becomes the fruit.
Stage 4. After pollination, part of the flower swells into a fruit. A tomato is a fruit because it holds seeds.
note.remember: If it has seeds inside, it's a fruit.

steps.title: Seeds inside
steps.instruction: Draw the seeds inside and the stem on top.

note.text: Each seed can grow into a new plant, so the cycle starts again.

steps.title: The cycle
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows from stage to stage, going clockwise.

note.text: The seeds inside the fruit grow into new plants, and the cycle starts again.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: These are a tomato plant's real colors, simplified.

steps.title: Stage order
steps.instruction: Tap the stages in order, starting from the seed.
steps.why: A seed sprouts into a seedling, grows into a flowering plant, and after pollination makes fruit with new seeds.
steps.hint: What has to happen before there can be fruit?

steps.title: Label the stages
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered stage.

targets.role: Holds the embryo and its food.
A young plant growing its first leaves and roots.

mistakes.Fruit: The fruit comes after the flower is pollinated. This is still the flower.

targets.role: Grows from the flower and holds the seeds.

commonMistakes.Spore: Ferns and mushrooms make spores. Flowering plants make seeds.
commonMistakes.Pupa: Pupa is an insect stage. Plants don't have one.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: What has to happen before a flower can turn into a fruit with seeds?

options.text: Pollen has to reach the flower (pollination)
options.feedback: Yes. Once pollinated, part of the flower grows into a fruit with seeds inside.

options.text: The flower has to lose its leaves
options.feedback: The plant keeps its leaves to make food. The fruit needs pollination.

options.text: The seeds have to sprout first
options.feedback: Seeds form inside the fruit, so they can't sprout before it exists.

options.text: Nothing; every flower becomes a fruit
options.feedback: Flowers that aren't pollinated usually wither without making fruit.
